about: Pairs of names for scoring ml_stack.graph.tidy's judge. Every name, definition and passage is invented -- an imagined field of glimmer nodes, vault currents and thrum coils -- so a score is about the judge and never about what a model happens to have memorised. `class` says what the pair is meant to test; `verdict` is the right answer; `passages` is what each name was read from, reachable through each side's provenance.

classes.same: the names alone settle it: a typo, a hyphenation, a capitalisation, a synonym
classes.different: the names alone settle it: an isomer-shaped pair, a numbered form, a subtype
classes.unsure-then-same: the names cannot settle it; the passages say they are one thing
classes.unsure-then-different: the names cannot settle it; the passages say they are two

a.label: glimmer node
a.definition: a point of the lattice that holds charge between pulses

passages.gold:glimmer-node: Each glimmer node holds charge between pulses. A lattice of glimmer nodes carries the charge from one rim to the other.
passages.gold:glimer-node: The glimer node holds charge between pulses, and a lattice of them carries it across.

a.label: flux-ring
a.definition: a closed loop of lattice that carries a standing current

passages.gold:flux-ring: A flux-ring is a closed loop of lattice carrying a standing current.
passages.gold:flux-ring-2: The flux ring, written with or without the hyphen, is the closed loop that carries the standing current.

a.label: Vault Current
a.definition: the current that runs the length of a vault

passages.gold:vault-current: The Vault Current runs the whole length of a vault and reverses at each rim.
passages.gold:vault-current-2: In the tables the vault current is given per rim rather than per vault.

a.label: thrum coil
a.definition: a winding that turns a vault current into a standing hum

passages.gold:thrum-coil: A thrum coil is the winding that turns a vault current into a standing hum.
passages.gold:thrumm-coil: The thrumm coil turns the vault current into a standing hum.

a.label: quill-bore
a.definition: the narrow channel cut through a lattice plate

passages.gold:quill-bore: The quill-bore is the narrow channel cut through a lattice plate.
passages.gold:quillbore: A quillbore, cut through the plate, is narrow enough to hold one thread of current.

a.label: sablon
a.definition: the grey mineral the lattice plates are ground from

passages.gold:sablon: Sablon is the grey mineral the lattice plates are ground from.
passages.gold:sablonn: Sablonn, the grey mineral, is ground into plates.

a.label: sylvane
a.definition: a light lattice binder with a single ring

b.label: sylvene
b.definition: a lattice binder with a double ring, which does not conduct

passages.gold:sylvane: Sylvane has one ring and conducts along the plate.
passages.gold:sylvene: Sylvene carries a second ring in place of the first bond, and conducts nothing; the pair are told apart by that ring alone.

a.label: flux ring 1
a.definition: the inner standing loop of a vault

b.label: flux ring 2
b.definition: the outer standing loop of a vault

passages.gold:flux-ring-1: Flux ring 1 is the inner loop, nearest the core.
passages.gold:flux-ring-2n: Flux ring 2 lies outside flux ring 1 and turns the other way.

a.label: kestrel-8B
a.definition: the eight-billion-weight reader used on the shelf

b.label: kestrel-8C
b.definition: a later reader of the same size with a different vocabulary

passages.gold:kestrel-8b: The kestrel-8B reader was measured over the whole shelf.
passages.gold:kestrel-8c: kestrel-8C is the same size as kestrel-8B but carries a different vocabulary and is scored apart from it.

a.label: marrow lattice
a.definition: the soft inner lattice of a vault plate

b.label: narrow lattice
b.definition: a lattice cut to less than one bore in width

passages.gold:marrow-lattice: The marrow lattice is the soft inner lattice of a plate.
passages.gold:narrow-lattice: A narrow lattice is any lattice cut to less than one bore across, whatever it is made of.

a.label: thrum coil
a.definition: the winding that turns a vault current into a standing hum

b.label: thrum core
b.definition: the sablon rod a thrum coil is wound around

passages.gold:thrum-coil-b: The thrum coil is the winding itself.
passages.gold:thrum-core: The thrum core is the sablon rod the coil is wound around; coil and core are fitted together but bought apart.

a.label: glimmer node
a.definition: a point of the lattice that holds charge

b.label: glimmer nodule
b.definition: a bead of spare sablon left on a plate after grinding

passages.gold:glimmer-node-b: A glimmer node holds charge at a point of the lattice.
passages.gold:glimmer-nodule: A glimmer nodule is a bead of spare sablon left on the plate after grinding; it holds no charge and is scraped off.

passages.gold:cinder-vault: A cinder vault is the housing that holds a stack of lattice plates.
passages.gold:cinder-vaulf: The cinder vaulf -- a misprint for cinder vault, corrected in the second edition -- holds a stack of plates.

passages.gold:glimmer-point: The glimmer point is what older editions call the glimmer node; the term was changed but the thing was not.
passages.gold:glimmer-node-c: A glimmer node holds charge at a point of the lattice.

passages.gold:vault-flux: Vault flux is the first edition's name for what this book calls the vault current; the two are one quantity, measured the same way.
passages.gold:vault-current-c: The vault current runs the length of a vault and reverses at each rim.

passages.gold:dram-coil: The dram coil is the short winding at the rim of a vault.
passages.gold:drum-coil: Chapter two prints drum coil for dram coil throughout; the same short rim winding is meant in both places.

passages.gold:tessel-loop: A tessel loop, or tessel ring, is the six-sided circuit cut into a plate; either name is used.
passages.gold:tessel-ring: The tessel ring is the six-sided circuit cut into a plate.

passages.gold:ember-lattice: The ember lattice is the warm-grade lattice used near a rim.
passages.gold:emberweave: Emberweave lattice is the trade name for the ember lattice; the plates are cut from the same stock to the same grade.

passages.gold:vault-current-d: The vault current runs the length of a vault from core to rim.
passages.gold:vault-countercurrent: The vault countercurrent is a separate flow running rim to core against the vault current; the two are measured on different rims and never summed.

passages.gold:ember-mesh: An ember mesh is a coarse screen laid over a plate to catch grinding dust; it holds no charge.
passages.gold:ember-lattice-d: The ember lattice is the warm-grade lattice that carries charge near a rim. It is not the mesh laid over it.

passages.gold:quill-bore-d: The quill bore is the narrow channel cut through a lattice plate.
passages.gold:quill-borer: The quill borer is the hand tool that cuts the bore; tool and hole are listed apart in the parts table.

passages.gold:tessel-ring-d: The tessel ring is the six-sided circuit cut into a plate.
passages.gold:tessel-ridge: The tessel ridge is the raised sablon rim standing around the ring; the ridge is what is ground away, the ring is what is kept.

passages.gold:pellum-drift: Pellum drift is the slow wander of a standing current across a plate over hours.
passages.gold:pellum-drag: Pellum drag is the loss a current takes crossing a bore, measured in the same units but at a single instant; drift and drag are reported in separate columns.

passages.gold:sablon-plate: A sablon plate is the ground disc the lattice is cut into.
passages.gold:sablon-platen: The sablon platen is the flat bed the plate is laid on while it is cut; one is the work and the other the bench.
